summary: The Lester B. Pearson International Scholarship is the University of Toronto's top award for international undergraduates. About 37 students are chosen each year for first-entry bachelor's study at the University of Toronto. A student cannot apply directly: their current secondary school must nominate them (one nominee per school), and they must then apply for admission and complete a scholarship application. The award pays tuition, books, incidental fees and full residence support for four years.
eligibility_notes:
You must be an international student, meaning a non-Canadian who needs a study permit. Canadian citizens, permanent residents and dual citizens are not eligible.

You must be in your final year of senior secondary school in 2026/2027, or have graduated no earlier than June 2026, and be starting undergraduate study at the University of Toronto in September 2027. You are not eligible if you are already in post-secondary study, or will start post-secondary study in January 2027 at the University of Toronto or anywhere else. You must apply to at least one University of Toronto first-entry undergraduate programme.

Nomination: only your current secondary school can nominate you, through an online process, and each school can nominate one student a year. Without a nomination you cannot be considered. A school that took part in the previous year does not need to sign up again; other schools apply to take part. The University of Toronto does not work with agents or third parties for this scholarship, and generative AI tools such as ChatGPT must not be used to create application content; breaking this rule leads to disqualification.

Selection looks for exceptional academic achievement, creativity, leadership within your school, and potential to contribute positively to the global community, with emphasis on your impact on school and community life. English language and school-level admission requirements are those of the University of Toronto admission process (not read in detail).
funding_summary: Covers tuition, books, incidental fees and full residence support for four years of first-entry undergraduate study at the University of Toronto. The inquiry page says visa fees, travel, relocation, living costs during breaks and the admission application fee are not covered.
programmes_note: Any first-entry undergraduate programme at the University of Toronto. You may list up to three programme areas in the admission application, but the scholarship applies only to your top choice at the time decisions are made.
institutions_note: Tenable only at the University of Toronto. Nomination comes from the student's secondary school, not from an embassy or agent.

requirements.text: Nomination from your current secondary school through the school's online nomination (one nominee per school per year). Schools that took part before get the nomination form from 6 July 2026; new schools could apply to take part by noon Eastern on 9 October 2026.

University of Toronto undergraduate admission application, submitted through the Ontario Universities' Application Centre (OUAC) by 16 October 2026, then documents uploaded in the Join U of T portal. The admission application fee is about CAD 180 and cannot be waived.

Pearson scholarship application and all required documentation, completed through a private link that your nominating school provides after you apply for admission. Deadline 6 November 2026. The pages I read do not list the individual documents; they are shown in the private link.
English proof as required for University of Toronto admission, unless exempt. The details are on the admission pages, which I did not read in full.
requirements.conditional_rule: If English is not your first language

application_steps.title: Ask your school to nominate you
application_steps.detail: Ask your counsellor, principal or head of school whether the school takes part. Schools that took part before receive the nomination form from 6 July 2026; other schools can apply to join by noon Eastern on 9 October 2026. The school nominates only one student per year and can nominate you before you apply to the University of Toronto.

application_steps.title: Apply for admission to the University of Toronto
application_steps.detail: Submit the OUAC application by 16 October 2026 for at least one first-entry undergraduate programme starting in September 2027. You can list up to three areas but the scholarship applies only to your top choice. You cannot submit the scholarship application until you have applied for admission.

application_steps.title: Complete the Pearson scholarship application
application_steps.detail: After you apply and are nominated, your school sends a private link to the scholarship application. Complete it and submit all required documentation by 6 November 2026. Do not use generative AI to create application content. The university says it does not use agents or third parties and warns against anyone who asks for fees or offers false acceptances.

application_steps.title: Competition among nominees
application_steps.detail: The school chooses its one top candidate, and the University of Toronto assesses nominees on exceptional academic achievement, creativity, leadership within the school and potential to contribute to the global community. About 37 Pearson Scholars are named each year (one section of the inquiry page says 38).

application_steps.title: Decisions
application_steps.detail: Recipients are notified from the end of January 2027 and all nominees are told by April 2027.

application_steps.title: Accept your place and begin in September 2027
application_steps.detail: Scholars start first-entry undergraduate study at the University of Toronto in September 2027. The page does not describe how to accept the scholarship; contact the Pearson team at the address the university gives for questions.

application_steps.title: Join the Pearson scholar programme
application_steps.detail: The Pearson Program Office runs a September orientation and welcome reception, one-to-one check-ins with an advisor every semester for all four years, a peer mentor in first year, a faculty mentor from second year, enrichment activities (leadership, careers, alumni networking, graduate school, entrepreneurship), a monthly social committee and an optional professional development plan. No renewal or performance conditions are stated.
